text:
Leah C.: Heads up — after last night's infra patch the Dedicated capacity console for cluster `eu-west-1:dedicated-3` is showing 0 nodes / 0 GPUs in the UI, but the node agent APIs still report healthy pods. Anyone else seeing inventory vanish? :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy-bot finished patch window for cluster eu-west-1 at 2025-11-07T03:12:09Z :information_source:

Samir P.: I can reproduce on my account. Console UI returns empty node array, metrics ingestion looks fine (kafka/metrics-consumer lag 0). My gut says a cache/namespace mismatch between inventory-service and the console frontend.

Leah C.: I ran a quick check on redis keys and the node counts are present: `redis-cli --raw keys "inventory:cluster:eu-west-1:dedicated-3:*"` returns keys and `GET inventory:cluster:eu-west-1:dedicated-3:nodes` -> `b\'10\'`. But curl to internal console API yields `200 {"nodes": []}`. Example curl:```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://console.internal/api/internal/inventory?cluster=eu-west-1:dedicated-3" | jq .``` shows empty array.

Ricardo M.: We rolled inventory-service v2.4.1 in the patch which renamed the redis namespace to `inventory:v2:`. Sounds like console still hitting old namespace endpoints (or vice versa). Could be an api-gateway/envoy route referencing `/v1/internal/inventory` -> inventory-service:v1. Check envoy config and the console's env var `INVENTORY_NAMESPACE`.

Samir P.: Quick mitigation: toggle the feature flag that switches console to v2 namespace so both sides align. Admin path: Settings -> Data -> Feature flags -> `inventory_v2_enabled`. Alternatively run `kubectl -n controlplane exec -it configstore -- consul kv delete config/console/INVENTORY_NAMESPACE` then set to `inventory:v2` — but that's destructive if wrong. Safer: toggle flag to false so console falls back to v1.

Leah C.: I toggled `inventory_v2_enabled` to false via the admin panel (didn't touch consul). UI now shows nodes and GPU counts again :white_check_mark:. Customer ticket T-3425 had been escalated for missing capacity in their dashboard; updated them with workaround.

Ricardo M.: Opening an incident PR and patching the routing config. Root cause looks like a deployment order bug: inventory-service started with v2 config while console schema rollout didn't coordinate feature flag. I'll add a post-deploy smoke check to the pipeline to hit `/internal/inventory?cluster=` immediately after infra changes. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge-requests/1289 (will add tests).

Support Ld: Noted — customer notified, they'll keep monitoring. Please add remediation steps to the runbook and tag the incident.

Samir P.: Quick repro steps for postmortem: 1) deploy inventory v2 with new namespace 2) do not flip `inventory_v2_enabled` on console 3) watch console return empty nodes while API and redis show data. Recorded logs: `console.ERROR inventory_fetch namespace not found -> returning []`.

Leah C.: Thanks — I'll start the incident note. We should schedule a controlled rollout tomorrow and add a migration script that mirrors keys between namespaces during the transition.
